item.title: About
item.description:
👋 Hi! I’m Xinyi Yi, a PhD student in Engineering at the University of Cambridge, Churchill College.
My research focuses on the optimal control and coordination of multi-energy systems, with a current emphasis on district heating networks, energy sharing, and data-driven temperature regulation.

I am currently supervised by Prof. Ioannis Lestas.
During my master’s at Tsinghua University, I worked under the guidance of Prof. Ye Guo, and during my undergraduate studies at North China Electric Power University, I was jointly advised by Prof. Cheng Yu and Prof. Ming Zhou.

item.title: Accepted at NECsys 2025 – Hong Kong
item.description:
🎉 Our paper “Optimal Energy-sharing and Temperature Regulation in District Heating Systems” has been accepted to NECsys 2025, to be held in Hong Kong, June 2–5, 2025.

📘 Abstract

We consider the problem of temperature regulation and optimal energy sharing in district heating systems without requiring any knowledge of the demand, while ensuring satisfactory transient performance.

We show that convex optimization problems can be formulated to jointly achieve optimal temperature regulation and energy sharing. Furthermore, we demonstrate that LQR formulations can asymptotically converge to these optimal operating points—while also minimizing transient performance metrics.

item.title: Research Overview
item.description:
🎯 A Closed-loop Vision: From Markets to Control and Back

My research explores how distributed control mechanisms can support real-world operation and pricing in multi-energy systems. I aim to bridge physical dynamics with market coordination, especially across electricity and heat sectors.

🔍 From Market Design to System Control

My academic journey began with the study of multi-energy system scheduling and market-based pricing mechanisms, particularly in electricity and district heating systems. During my undergraduate and master’s training, I focused on how coordinated optimization of electricity and heat flows could support more efficient and equitable energy market pricing, including energy and reserve markets.
